(a) Find all values of \(t\) in the interval \(2 \leq t \leq 4\) for which the speed of the particle is 2 .
(b) Write an expression involving an integral that gives the position \(s(t)\). Use this expression to find the

(d) Is the speed of the particle increasing or decreasing at time \(t=4\) ? Give a reason for your answer.

\section*{Question 2}

A particle moves along a straight line. For \(0 \leq t \leq 5\), the velocity of the particle is given by
\(v(t)=-2+\left(t^{2}+3 t\right)^{6 / 5}-t^{3}\), and the position of the particle is given by \(s(t)\). It is known that \(s(0)=10\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find all values of \(t\) in the interval \(2 \leq t \leq 4\) for which the speed of the particle is 2.
\item[(b)] Write an expression involving an integral that gives the position \(s(t)\). Use this expression to find the position of the particle at time \(t=5\).
\item[(c)] Find all times \(t\) in the interval \(0 \leq t \leq 5\) at which the particle changes direction. Justify your answer.
\item[(d)] Is the speed of the particle increasing or decreasing at time \(t=4\) ? Give a reason for your answer.
\item[(a)] Solve \(|v(t)|=2\) on \(2 \leq t \leq 4\).
\(t=3.128\) (or 3.127) and \(t=3.473\)
\item[(b)] \(s(t)=10+\int_{0}^{t} v(x) d x\)
\(s(5)=10+\int_{0}^{5} v(x) d x=-9.207\)
\item[(c)] \(\quad v(t)=0\) when \(t=0.536033,3.317756\)
\(v(t)\) changes sign from negative to positive at time \(t=0.536033\).
\(v(t)\) changes sign from positive to negative at time \(t=3.317756\).
Therefore, the particle changes direction at time \(t=0.536\) and time \(t=3.318\) (or 3.317).
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { considers }|v(t)|=2 \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: s(t) \\ 1: s(5)\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { considers } v(t)=0 \\ 2: \text { answers with justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[2] : conclusion with reason
\item[(d)] \(v(4)=-11.475758<0, a(4)=v^{\prime}(4)=-22.295714<0\)
The speed is increasing at time \(t=4\) because velocity and acceleration have the same sign.
\end{itemize}
